report_name: TIAA Discloses Data Breach Exposing Client SSNs

threat_actors.name: TIAA Breach Attacker
threat_actors.description: The unknown threat actor responsible for the data breach at TIAA in September 2026, which resulted in the theft of client names and Social Security numbers.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Information Repositories
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor acquired client names and Social Security numbers from TIAA's internal data stores, such as databases or file shares.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor exfiltrated the stolen names and Social Security numbers from TIAA's network to an external location.

identities.name: TIAA
identities.description: A U.S. financial services organization that suffered a data breach resulting in the compromise of client names and Social Security numbers.

indicators.name: Database Client Execution on Non-Standard Systems
indicators.pattern:
title: Database Client Execution on Non-Standard Systems
id: 2b1c8e9f-4d5a-4b6c-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of database client tools (e.g., sqlcmd, psql), which could indicate unauthorized database access or reconnaissance, especially when run from non-administrator or non-server workstations.
references:
  - https://www.claimdepot.com/data-breach/tiaa-2026
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-05
tags:
  - attack.t1213
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\sqlcmd.exe'
      - '\psql.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use by database administrators or developers on their workstations.
indicators.description: Detects the use of database client tools (e.g., sqlcmd, psql) from non-administrator workstations, a potential indicator of data theft reconnaissance.

relationships.source_name: Database Client Execution on Non-Standard Systems
